correctness.rationale: The branching generating-function backward equations are F_i=r_i*p_i-b*p_i^2+m sum_neigh(p_j-p_i)=0. A birth-death stochastic comparison bounds all positive survival probabilities away from 0 and 1; the max-ratio argument makes the positive solution unique. If p1=p2=t, the endpoint forces t=r1/b, the center imposes m(z-t)=(r1-r2)t, and the third component gives b z^2-r3 z+(r1-r2)t=0 with unique root z<t by 2r1>r2+r3. Continuity and small/large migration signs yield precisely one crossing; endpoint comparisons exclude any tie with the poorest site. Two sites cannot switch with common birth rate. Independent rational witness b=10, r=(6,8,1), m=6, p=(3/5,3/5,2/5) has exactly zero three-equation residual.
